# 629. Characterizing discrete sets generated by fixed-parameter extrapolation

**Area:** Discrete geometry and aperiodic order

**Status:** ✅ SOLVED

**Last checked:** 2026-10-15

## Problem statement

For $`\lambda\in\mathbb C`$, let $`Q_\lambda`$ be the smallest subset of $`\mathbb C`$ containing $`0,1`$ and closed under the operation

```math
a\star_\lambda b=(1-\lambda)a+\lambda b.
```

Only finitely many operations are used to generate each point; no topological closure is taken.

Call $`\lambda`$ a **strong PV number** if it is an algebraic integer and every Galois conjugate other than $`\lambda`$ and $`\overline\lambda`$ lies in the real interval $`(0,1)`$. This definition includes integers and nonreal quadratic algebraic integers.

Prove or disprove that $`Q_\lambda`$ is discrete if and only if $`\lambda`$ is a strong PV number. For these generated sets, discreteness is equivalent to uniform discreteness: there exists $`\delta>0`$ such that distinct $`x,y\in Q_\lambda`$ satisfy $`|x-y|\ge\delta`$.

## Application

The operation models point generation in quasicrystal constructions. A characterization would identify exactly which parameters produce separated geometric structures rather than arbitrarily fine point patterns.

## References

1. S. Fenner, F. Green and S. Homer, [Fixed-Parameter Extrapolation and Aperiodic Order](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-025-00816-4), *Discrete & Computational Geometry* **76** (2026), 1–74, Definition 4.1, Theorem 4.12 and Conjecture 11.1.
2. S. Fenner, F. Green and S. Homer, [Extended manuscript](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.2889).

## Status review

Reviewed 15 October 2026 against the original target in [PR #111](https://github.com/MColbrook/AIM/pull/111). Discreteness of the finite extrapolation set is equivalent to the full strong-PV conjugate condition.

[Proof or source](../research/solutions/629-extrapolation-discreteness/paper/extrapolation_discreteness.pdf) · [Independent AI review](../research/solution_reviews/2026-10-15-active-prs/629-review.md). The linked review records the target comparison.

**Scope:** For every complex parameter, Q_lambda is discrete exactly when lambda is a strong PV algebraic integer; the proof also gives pairwise separation at least1 in that case.

### Earlier review notes

The following historical notes are retained; the current decision and review date are given above.

**Known cases:** Strong PV parameters give uniformly discrete sets. Discreteness also forces the parameter to be an algebraic integer.

**Remaining target:** Prove the full restriction on all other Galois conjugates, or construct a discrete generated set whose parameter is not strong PV. The June 2026 journal version explicitly retains this converse as a conjecture.
